mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for two consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which historically precedes slower earnings growth and higher input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to lower earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous year for 3 consecutive months, with monthly drop > -0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 3% while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is simultaneously rising above 4% signals a monetary policy shock that increases uncertainty and reduces risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps > 0.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 4% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) below 50,000 for two consecutive months signals a stalling labor market, which historically precedes flat or declining corporate earnings and thus negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced revenue expectations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.3% for four consecutive months, regardless of regime, is a reliable always-on leading indicator of negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated earnings compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes over any 5-year rolling window.
